baseline: Host LTP 20260529 prebuilt (/nix/store/hik6kb512ia3p14lc2vwzb292d4k306a-ltp-20260529/testcases/bin/times03) on Linux 6.8.0-124-generic: 12 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken / 0 skipped. Per assertion, the correct kernel returns: (1) times03.c:89 buf1.tms_utime <= 5 and :94 buf1.tms_stime <= 5 -- a freshly forked child has near-zero accumulated CPU time, and crucially the field is *written* by the kernel rather than left as caller garbage; (2) :105 buf2.tms_utime != 0 (host 134 ticks) and :118 buf2.tms_stime != 0 (host 175) after the test burns ~1s of user time in a spin loop and ~2s of system time in a times() call loop; (3) :111 buf1.tms_utime < buf2.tms_utime (0 < 134) and :124 buf1.tms_stime < buf2.tms_stime (0 < 175) -- strict monotonic growth of self CPU time; (4) :131 buf2.tms_cutime == 0 and :136 buf2.tms_cstime == 0 -- no child has been reaped yet, so the children fields must read exactly zero, which also requires them to be written rather than left as garbage; (5) :155 buf2.tms_utime <= buf3.tms_utime (134 <= 134) and :163 buf2.tms_stime <= buf3.tms_stime (175 <= 175) -- self time is non-decreasing and, per POSIX, is NOT inflated by the child's usage; (6) :170 buf3.tms_cutime != 0 (host 147) and :175 buf3.tms_cstime != 0 (host 252) -- after SAFE_WAITPID reaps the forked child, the child's user and system time appear in the parent's cutime/cstime. All four fields and the return value are in USER_HZ clock ticks (getconf CLK_TCK = 100 on the host, i.e. 10ms per tick), not in the kernel's internal 1000Hz jiffies. times() returns elapsed wall-clock ticks since an arbitrary epoch and only fails with EFAULT on an unwritable buf; buf == NULL is permitted on Linux and returns just the tick count.
failing_assertion: 8 of 12 assertions fail in Asterinas at e8f2b9ca6 (4 passed / 8 failed / 0 broken / 0 skipped), reproduced across three boots via CONFORMANCE_TEST_SELECTOR=times03. The buffer is never written, so every field reads back uninitialized stack garbage: 'times03.c:87: TFAIL: buf1.tms_utime = 206158430240' (0x3000000020) and 'times03.c:92: TFAIL: buf1.tms_stime = 140737487956384' (0x7FFFFFFFE060, a stack address) instead of values <= 5; 'times03.c:103: TFAIL: buf2.tms_utime = 0' and 'times03.c:116: TFAIL: buf2.tms_stime = 0' instead of nonzero; 'times03.c:108: TFAIL: buf1.tms_utime (206158430240) >= buf2.tms_utime (0)' and 'times03.c:121: TFAIL: buf1.tms_stime (140737487956384) >= buf2.tms_stime (0)' -- the monotonicity checks invert because the garbage in buf1 happens to exceed the garbage in buf2; 'times03.c:134: TFAIL: buf2.tms_cstime = 4320994' instead of 0; 'times03.c:173: TFAIL: buf3.tms_cstime = 0' instead of nonzero. The 4 incidental passes (buf2.tms_cutime = 0, the two buf2<=buf3 comparisons, buf3.tms_cutime = 4363984) are accidents of whatever the stack happened to hold and carry no information. Root evidence for the mechanism, captured directly from the kernel log at LOG_LEVEL=warn: 'WARN: Unimplemented syscall number: 100' appears at the exact point times03 starts, 100 being __NR_times on x86-64.
root_cause: sys_times is not implemented anywhere in Asterinas. No handler exists (a repo-wide grep for sys_times/SYS_TIMES across *.rs finds only unrelated utimensat text) and neither dispatch table registers the number: kernel/src/syscall/arch/x86.rs goes from SYS_GETRUSAGE = 98 (line 278) and SYS_SYSINFO = 99 (line 279) straight to SYS_PTRACE = 101 (line 280), skipping 100; kernel/src/syscall/arch/generic.rs jumps SYS_SETFSGID = 152 (line 337) to SYS_SETPGID = 154 (line 338), skipping the riscv/arm64 number 153. An unregistered number falls to the `_ =>` arm of syscall_dispatch in kernel/src/syscall/mod.rs:337-343, which logs 'Unimplemented syscall number: {}' at warn level and returns ENOSYS. The consequence is specifically a silent-garbage failure rather than a clean error, because of how glibc's times() wrapper handles it: the wrapper reports failure only for EFAULT, so an ENOSYS return is not surfaced as -1 to the caller. times03 therefore takes the success path at lines 83, 99 and 148 without ever entering the tst_brk branch, and reads a struct tms that the kernel never touched -- the caller's uninitialized stack. That is why the observed values are a stack address and a small heap-ish constant rather than zeros, and it also explains why the sibling times01 (already enabled at all.txt line 1706) passes today: times01 only checks TST_RET == -1 and never inspects the buffer, so it passes vacuously against an unimplemented syscall. times03 is the first test that actually reads the fields.
invariant: times() must write all four fields of struct tms into the caller's buffer on every successful return, in USER_HZ clock ticks: tms_utime/tms_stime are the calling process's whole-thread-group accumulated user and kernel CPU time, and tms_cutime/tms_cstime are the summed user and kernel CPU time of children already reaped via wait(). Self times must be non-decreasing across calls and must never absorb a child's usage; children times must read exactly zero until the first child is reaped, and must become nonzero once one has been. A syscall that cannot supply these values must not leave the buffer untouched while reporting success, because the caller cannot distinguish an unwritten buffer from a legitimately zero one.
owning_layer: The syscall-entry layer: a new sys_times handler in kernel/src/syscall/times.rs, registered as SYS_TIMES = 100 in kernel/src/syscall/arch/x86.rs and SYS_TIMES = 153 in kernel/src/syscall/arch/generic.rs. This is the correct layer because the accounting itself already lives below and is live, not stubbed: kernel/src/process/process/timer_manager.rs:66-71 adds a jiffy to both the per-thread and per-process user or kernel CpuClock on every timer interrupt depending on the interrupted privilege level, and kernel/src/process/wait.rs:369-372 accumulates a reaped child's totals into the parent's ReapedChildrenStats. So no new state or bookkeeping is needed anywhere; the only thing missing is a syscall that reads the existing per-process ProfClock and ReapedChildrenStats and marshals them into one 4-field struct. Asterinas has no VFS-style intermediate layer here and needs none -- Linux's own do_sys_times is likewise a thin reader in kernel/sys.c, not a subsystem.
linux_reference: kernel/sys.c: do_sys_times(struct tms *tms) reads self time via thread_group_cputime_adjusted(current, &tgutime, &tgstime) and the children totals straight out of current->signal->cutime / current->signal->cstime (unlocked in current mainline; older kernels held signal->siglock), then converts each of the four with nsec_to_clock_t(). SYSCALL_DEFINE1(times, struct tms __user *, tbuf) writes the struct only when tbuf is non-NULL, returns -EFAULT if copy_to_user fails, and otherwise calls force_successful_syscall_return() and returns jiffies_64_to_clock_t(get_jiffies_64()). The USER_HZ conversion is the load-bearing detail for Asterinas: nsec_to_clock_t in kernel/time/time.c reduces to div_u64(x, NSEC_PER_SEC / USER_HZ) = div_u64(x, 10000000) when USER_HZ is 100, and jiffies_64_to_clock_t reduces to div_u64(x, HZ / USER_HZ) = div_u64(x, 10) for HZ=1000. Linux enforces the rule in the syscall entry itself, which is where Asterinas should also enforce it. Note that Linux populates tms_cutime/tms_cstime only at wait() reap time (per times(2)), so grandchildren a child never waited for are never counted -- Asterinas's ReapedChildrenStats already matches this by construction.
other_callers: Nobody else reaches this defect, because the handler does not exist -- there is exactly one entry point and no shared code path to regress. The state it must read is, however, already exposed through two existing readers that are green and must stay green, and they are the reference for correctness: sys_getrusage (kernel/src/syscall/getrusage.rs:26-52) reads the same process ProfClock user/kernel clocks for RUSAGE_SELF and the same reaped_children_stats().lock().get() for RUSAGE_CHILDREN, though it reports timeval rather than ticks; and procfs /proc/<pid>/stat (kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/procfs/pid/task/stat.rs:178-196) builds exactly the utime/stime/cutime/cstime quadruple this syscall needs. A fix at the syscall layer cannot disturb either. The one caveat worth flagging for the next phase is that both existing readers work in raw 1000Hz jiffies (procfs stat emits read_jiffies().as_u64() and duration_to_jiffies() at stat.rs:349-356, with TIMER_FREQ = 1000 in ostd/src/timer/mod.rs:25), so copying their arithmetic verbatim would report ticks 10x too large for a userspace CLK_TCK of 100. sys_times must divide down to USER_HZ.
suggested_direction: Add kernel/src/syscall/times.rs with a `#[repr(C)] #[derive(Pod)] struct tms_t { tms_utime: i64, tms_stime: i64, tms_cutime: i64, tms_cstime: i64 }` (clock_t is i64 on 64-bit, matching the existing `pub type clock_t = i64` in kernel/src/process/signal/c_types.rs:18). In sys_times(buf_addr, ctx): take ctx.process.prof_clock().user_clock()/kernel_clock() for tms_utime/tms_stime and ctx.process.reaped_children_stats().lock().get() for tms_cutime/tms_cstime -- the same two sources getrusage.rs already uses, so process-wide semantics come for free and no new locking is introduced beyond the one Mutex getrusage already takes. Convert every field to USER_HZ = 100 ticks, not raw jiffies: derive from Duration (read_time()) or divide the jiffy count by TIMER_FREQ / USER_HZ = 10, and add a shared helper rather than open-coding the divisor, since procfs stat.rs deliberately wants raw jiffies and must not change. Following Linux, write the struct only when buf_addr is non-zero via ctx.user_space().write_val(), let the write's Err propagate as EFAULT, and return elapsed wall-clock time in USER_HZ ticks -- Jiffies::elapsed().as_u64() / 10 -- rather than 0, since the return value is part of the contract even though times03 ignores it. Register SYS_TIMES = 100 => sys_times(args[..1]) in x86.rs between lines 279 and 280, SYS_TIMES = 153 in generic.rs between lines 337 and 338, add the `mod times;` declaration in kernel/src/syscall/mod.rs beside `mod getrusage;` (line 72) and the `times::sys_times` import beside getrusage's at x86.rs:58. Then uncomment `# times03` at test/initramfs/src/conformance/ltp/testcases/all.txt line 1707. Two traps to respect: assertion :155/:163 require that a reaped child's CPU time is NOT added to the parent's own tms_utime/tms_stime (only to cutime/cstime), which the separate ProfClock and ReapedChildrenStats already give correctly -- do not sum them; and assertions :131/:136 require cutime/cstime to be exactly 0 before any reap, so the fields must be written unconditionally rather than skipped when the stats are empty. Leave times01 alone: it passes vacuously today and will keep passing once the syscall is real.
